broken.name: The X-feed collector (MacBook)
broken.since: last good publish Fri 25 Sep 16:31 ET

items.name: The doorman (chart API, 2 machines)
items.line: Answering; both machines report ready.

items.name: The gatekeeper at the bar door (bar service)
items.line: Running on the 09:00 ET image; relative volume written after Friday's close.

items.name: The stream listener
items.line: Beating every 30 seconds; marked minutes through Friday 19:59 ET (market closed since).

items.name: Friday evening intraday bars
items.line: From about 16:20 to 20:00 ET Friday the extended-hours bars were reported behind. Handed to Q2a. The warning is still showing because it only clears during market hours.

items.name: The 4-minute Geiger robot
items.line: Published 590 of 590 names, 4,130 rungs, VERIFIED (last at 15:20 UTC).

items.name: This morning's hold
items.line: From 06:13 to 08:57 ET it refused 42 times in a row and the Hub kept showing the last full reading. Nothing alarmed. Q2a owns the cause.

items.name: The closing-bell clerk
items.line: Waiting: there is no trading session today.

items.name: The scout and the seven-rung scout
items.line: Both fired on their minute this hour; Friday's readings were written at 20:17 and 20:21 ET.

items.name: The fan clerk (REWIND)
items.line: Fired on time; 586 of 590 names have a row for each day since 29 Sep (4 a day are missing, which its rule allows; sent to Q2a).

items.name: The night copyist (long chart histories)
items.line: Friday night's pass refreshed the long copies; today it skips (weekend).

items.name: The night watchman (second opinion)
items.line: Not running yet. It is built on Q2a's branch and will report here once Alan approves it.

items.name: The backup clerks
items.line: All three nightly copies ran; the backup check found 4 tables short. The worst is the REWIND history, missing 1,080,400 of 1,230,600 rows in the backup.

items.name: The backup repairman
items.line: Has not sent a single repair in at least 14 nights. Its own pauses are longer than the database allows, so every run is cancelled and undone. Fix written, waiting for Alan.

items.name: The news wire
items.line: New headlines every minute.

items.name: The news-mood reader
items.line: On the :40 run in 4 of the last 6 hours, it could not read the news table. The :50 run caught up. Nothing recorded these errors until today.

items.name: The X-feed collector (MacBook)
items.line: Dead. Its program folder was deleted on 28 Sep, so it cannot start, and nobody was told. The newest X post we hold is from 27 Sep.
items.since: last good publish Fri 25 Sep 16:31 ET

items.name: The X-mood reader
items.line: It reports success every 2 hours but has had nothing to read since 28 Sep, because its source is the dead collector.

items.name: The YouTube scouts
items.line: Videos refreshed this hour.

items.name: The statistics clerk (STATS)
items.line: Only 6 to 26% of its runs reach the function since 28 Sep. They fire at :00 and :30 together with about 20 other jobs, and are cut off after 5 seconds. Fix written: move it to :13 and :43.

items.name: The daily ribbon painter
items.line: 23 to 35% of its runs get through since 29 Sep, for the same reason (the quarter-hour rush). The ribbons are still fresh, because about one run in four lands.

items.name: Put/call (IB, MacBook)
items.line: The counter is running; Friday's last minute arrived at 15:59 ET. Market closed.

items.name: Prediction markets, analysts, dilution, lock-ups, sigma
items.line: Every nightly reader wrote its table on its last scheduled night.

items.name: The dead-man's switch (job heartbeat)
items.line: Watching 150 jobs every 5 minutes, but its alarms are off. It went live this morning before the "nothing without Alan" rule. Keeping it, and switching its alarms on, both need Alan's yes.

items.name: The old alert writer
items.line: 9,352 alerts stored and none ever delivered. Nothing new since 18 Sep.

items.name: Weekend warnings
items.line: Three warnings are stuck on red until Monday: two froze when their market-hours window closed, and one cannot tell a weekend from an outage.
